post.caption: Tungsten means heavy stone in Swedish. English borrowed it from the old Swedish name of a heavy mineral. Sweden itself calls the metal volfram. Its symbol W comes from the name wolfram. Tungsten melts above 3,400 degrees Celsius, hotter than any other metal. Pure tungsten is almost exactly as dense as gold. Rings use tungsten carbide, which starts as powder pressed in a mold. It is baked until a binder glues the grains together. The finished ring rates about 9 on the Mohs scale. It acts like a ceramic, so it cannot be resized. In 1962, Rado launched a scratchproof watch with a tungsten carbide case.
